Summary  
The “data source” supplied for extraction is not a normal article but only the bibliography / reference list of a larger paper. Because it contains no prose, arguments, empirical results, design descriptions, theoretical analyses, or proposed interventions, there is no explicit or implicit causal-interventional reasoning pathway that can be traced from top-level risks through intermediate concept categories to actionable interventions. Every entry is merely a citation pointer to some other work; none of the required information for node creation (claims, methods, findings, mechanisms, validations, interventions) is present in the text itself. Consequently, constructing even a single connected risk→…→intervention pathway without resorting to pure speculation is impossible.  

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[9]  
(The very low confidence reflects the impossibility of meeting the mandatory success criteria with the material provided.)  

Inference strategy justification  
Only minimal inference was attempted (verifying whether any citation titles alone could justify nodes). Titles alone are far too thin to support even “weak” (confidence 2) edges because no contextual detail is available. Creating a knowledge fabric on that basis would violate the instruction to prioritise accuracy and traceability to “closest preceding data source section titles.” There are no such sections—only citation lines—so every edge would be purely speculative (confidence 1) and un-traceable. Therefore, the correct action is to report that extraction is not feasible rather than fabricate unsupported nodes.

Extraction completeness explanation  
All possibilities in the text were examined; none provide the minimum information required to instantiate the six concept-node categories or any intervention node. Hence the output is complete in the sense that it faithfully represents the total absence of extractable causal content in this source.

Key limitations  
1. Bibliographic lists are not suitable primary sources for knowledge-fabric extraction; the pipeline needs access to the full paper content.  
2. Automatic detection of “reference-only” documents would save processing time.  
3. Future instructions could specify fallback behaviours (e.g., locate and ingest the cited works automatically) when a source lacks extractable pathways.
